title: Each CodeBlock line number widens its own row, so the code shifts right at rows 10 and 100
foundBy: consumer report from the campaign repository's review page (SAC-095), filed at the user's request

evidence.verified: At 0f753c2, `npx vitest run --project browser src/components/CodeBlock.layout.test.tsx` passed 4 of 4. In a 120-line block, the code on lines 1, 9, 10, 99, 100 and 120 starts at 49.39 px. That holds in the default, `fillHeight` and `inline` modes alike. Line 1's number measures 32.80, 40.59 and 48.39 px wide in blocks of 9, 10 and 100 lines, one digit apart. With the style removed from `<code>`, all 4 tests failed, and the code moved from 33.81 to 41.61 px at line 10. With the digit count pinned to 1, the rows stayed aligned and the sizing test failed. `npm run visual:compare` passed 116/116 against the re-recorded captures with no new axe findings, and `npm run check` passed 820 of 820 tests.

resolution: Every line number in a block takes one width, as many `ch` as the last line number has digits, in every mode. CodeBlock writes the digit count to `--code-block-gutter-digits` on its `<code>`, and the number's content box is that many `ch` wide. The `min-width: 3ch` it replaces never applied, because the padding alone was wider. Captures of blocks under ten lines did not change.
details:
Each line of a CodeBlock is a flex row of its own, and its number sits in a span with `min-width: 3ch` in `src/styles/components/code-block.css`. The same span has `padding-left: var(--space-4)` and `padding-right: var(--space-2)` under `box-sizing: border-box`. The padding alone is wider than `3ch`, so the minimum never applies, and each number is as wide as its own digits. A row with more digits pushes its code further right.

To reproduce, render a CodeBlock of 120 lines in any mode and read `getBoundingClientRect().left` of the code span on lines 9, 10 and 100. In a consumer at a 1600 pixel viewport they read 313.8, 321.6 and 329.4. The code moves one character width, 7.8 pixels, at line 10 and again at line 100.

A consumer can correct this only by reaching into the component's markup, because the line number has no documented hook. A gutter sized once for the whole block, from the digit count of its last line, would keep every row aligned.
